subject: [PATCH v2 1/3] mm: page_alloc: add a watermark check that knows the migratetype

2026-11-02.patch_summary: This patch adds a watermark check to the Linux kernel's page allocation system that takes into account the migratetype of the request. The high-order check in __zone_watermark_ok() previously accepted free pages of any migratetype, which could lead to incorrect results under ALLOC_NOFRAGMENT. To fix this, the patch introduces a new function __zone_watermark_ok_mt() that considers only the pages it can take based on the request's migratetype. This change affects various parts of the kernel, including the allocator fast path, recheck after node reclaim, and compaction's up-front check.

reviews.author: Harry Yoo
reviews.summary:
Reviewer Harry Yoo noted that __zone_watermark_ok() needs to account for defrag_mode, where allocations cannot steal pages from other migrate types, and suggested adding a concise changelog entry to explain this requirement.

Reviewer Harry Yoo noted that the patch does not handle the case where the migratetype is not specified, and suggested adding a check to ensure this condition is handled.
reviews.raw_body:
nit: perhaps we could make the changelog above bit more concise.

I think the necessary bit here is "With defrag_mode, allocations cannot
steal a page from pageblocks of other migrate type, thus
__zone_watermark_ok() needs to take that into account."

... and maybe

- "Ignoring the allocation's migrate type leads to
   stopping direct compaction and reclamation prematurely".

- "Indirect compaction and reclamation are not affected as they do not
   serve specific allocations"

---

otherwise looks good to me,
Reviewed-by: Harry Yoo (Meta) <harry@kernel.org>

with a nit below.

2026-11-05.patch_summary: This patch modifies the page allocation watermark check in the Linux kernel to take into account the migratetype of the request. The high-order check in __zone_watermark_ok() previously accepted a free page of any migratetype, which could lead to incorrect results under ALLOC_NOFRAGMENT. To fix this, the patch introduces a new function __zone_watermark_ok_mt() that takes the migratetype as an argument and is used by various parts of the kernel, including the allocator fast path, recheck after node reclaim, and compaction's up-front check. This change ensures that the watermark check accurately reflects the available memory for each migratetype.

reviews.author: Kiryl Shutsemau (author)
reviews.summary:
The author addressed a concern about the specific conditions under which ALLOC_NOFRAGMENT allocations can claim whole free pageblocks of another migratetype, clarifying that it is only when DMA32 is populated and defrag_mode is off.

Author addressed a concern that kcompactd_node_suitable() does not pass the migratetype to __zone_watermark_ok_mt(), explaining that it uses MIGRATE_MOVABLE which is only read under ALLOC_NOFRAGMENT, and confirmed that no functional change has been introduced yet.
reviews.raw_body:
It is ALLOC_NOFRAGMENT, not defrag_mode: Normal zone allocations get it
on the first attempt when DMA32 is populated, with defrag_mode off. And
such an allocation can still claim a whole free pageblock of another
migratetype.

But fair, it can be shorter. A tighter version is below; it also says
why kcompactd passes MIGRATE_MOVABLE.

---

The value is not read there: __zone_watermark_ok_mt() uses the
migratetype only under ALLOC_NOFRAGMENT, and kcompactd never passes it.
kcompactd_node_suitable() makes the same call and has no compact_control
to take it from.

Thanks for the review.

The new changelog:

	The high-order check in __zone_watermark_ok() accepts a free page of any
	migratetype.  Under ALLOC_NOFRAGMENT, a request below pageblock_order can
	only take a page of its own migratetype or claim a whole free block, so
	the check can pass when the allocation cannot succeed.

	Only a check whether one allocation can be served now should count just
	the pages it can take.  A check whether a zone has enough free memory
	serves no single allocation and counts every migratetype: reclaim and
	compaction free whole pageblocks across migratetypes.

	Add __zone_watermark_ok_mt(), which takes the migratetype, for the first
	kind:

	  - the allocator fast path, zone_watermark_fast();
	  - its recheck after node reclaim in get_page_from_freelist();
	  - compaction's up-front check, compaction_suit_allocation_order().

	__zone_watermark_ok() wraps it for the second kind.  kcompactd shares
	compaction_suit_allocation_order() with direct compaction and passes
	MIGRATE_MOVABLE, which is not read without ALLOC_NOFRAGMENT.

	Declare both in mm/internal.h: nothing outside mm uses them.

	Nothing reads the migratetype yet: no functional change.  Preparation for
	making the high-order check honour ALLOC_NOFRAGMENT.

Looks good?

-- 
  Kiryl Shutsemau / Kirill A. Shutemov
